title: I built a place to publish the HTML games people are creating with AI
author: DonkeyFar5962
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting a lot with creating small games using ChatGPT and other AI tools.

And I kept running into the same problem:

Making the game is becoming incredibly easy.

But once you have the HTML file… where do you actually put it?

So I started building **Zyplo.io**.

The idea is simple: upload an HTML game and instantly have a place where people can discover it and play it directly from their phone.

No installs. No app store. Just open and play.

I’m especially interested in what happens now that almost anyone can describe a game to an AI and get something playable back.

Zyplo is still evolving, so I’d genuinely like feedback from people building games this way.

What would you want from a platform like this?

[**zyplo.io**](http://zyplo.io)

Made a game? **Zyplo it.**

comments.author: Brewgazer
comments.body: I did the same thing with flashvibegames.com got the idea when I realized I like making flash style edgy games and needed a place where the use of ai wasn’t hated on

replies.author: DonkeyFar5962
replies.body:
sounds like we arrived at a similar idea from different angles.

I also think there’s a growing group of people who enjoy making weird, experimental, small games with AI and just want a place to publish them without immediately getting judged for the tools they used.

I’ll check out flashvibegames.com. Thanks for sharing it.

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Yeah man! It’s all about finding game loops that work first and building off the game loops/systems to make a bigger game. I actually find it really fun to do this, I started using certain skills for blender to create huge open worlds where I take parts of real life cities. It’s pretty insane the kinda systems you can create and then save as skills so it’s easier to utilize later on down the line

replies.author: DonkeyFar5962
replies.body: same here I honestly have a lot of fun just creating simples games too. Like pacman or tetris with my style.

comments.author: Psychological-Key-36
comments.body: How does the game discovery work? What decides which game is shown first? Is it random? Do players need to scroll past 50 games to find mine? Is there popularity ranking? Quality ranking? Can we rate games? How are you dealing with localization? Most of the games are Spanish.

replies.author: DonkeyFar5962
replies.body:
Great questions. Discovery is something I’m still tuning.

The idea is definitely not “upload a game and hope someone scrolls through 50 others to find it” There are rankings, ratings, and signals around engagement to help surface games, and I want new games to still have a real chance to be discovered.

Localization is also something I need to improve. Right now a lot of the early games are in Spanish simply because many of the first creators are Spanish-speaking, but the goal is for Zyplo to be global and make language much less of a barrier.

Really useful feedback btw — these are exactly the things I’m trying to improve.  
Thx!
